outcome: Retained evolution/row-FFT fusion. Default median GPU time fell from 7.0648 ms to 6.6203 ms (6.29%) in eight interleaved runs; all tested float32 rows and rendered images match exactly.

implementation.workgroup: 128 threads evolve two samples each directly into the original bit-reversed float4 threadgroup arrays, then execute the unchanged row butterfly operations.
implementation.default: Fused; fusedEvolution=0 selects the original SIM_EVOLVE then FFT_ROWS chain.
implementation.resources: Original spectrum buffers are allocated only in the reference mode. Diagnostics report actual combined buffer lengths under spectrumBufferBytes.
implementation.trafficScope: Counts logical writes and reads of the two eliminated float4 spectrum buffers. It does not measure DRAM traffic, cache misses, or power.
implementation.precision: No half conversion or lower precision is introduced. The original float32 evolution body and butterfly implementation are copied without arithmetic changes. The spectrum buffer boundary itself did not change precision.
implementation.sourceAudit: The original evolution body matches the helper after changing output destinations and return value; the original bit-reversal/butterfly source is unchanged. Every preexisting native shader still matches the pre-fusion source hash.

initialPrototypeComparison.note: Eight preliminary runs before removing the unused intermediate allocations; final comparisons above use the zero-allocation fused path.

validation.fullSuite: zsh macos/test.sh completed successfully with twelve PASS gates; log: macos/build/evolution-validation.log
validation.metalValidation: Metal API and shader validation passed on the portrait GPU target with the fused path and no intermediate spectrum buffers.
validation.allocationChecks: All final benchmark runs and isolated image comparisons assert 12 MiB in the two-pass reference and zero bytes in the fused path.

interpretation: Median GPU reductions are 6.29% default, 5.97% after the stable-clock handover, 5.98% portrait and 5.95% ultrawide. CPU results vary by case; no general CPU or energy improvement is claimed.
limitations: Single Apple M1; software viewport targets do not establish results on every physical monitor or GPU generation.
Sixteen deterministic synthetic row tests and twelve rendered states cover tested inputs, rather than every possible setting or phase.
The row oracle compares the actual two-pass reference with the fused kernel; it does not introduce an independent ocean model. Butterfly arithmetic is unchanged.
GPU command-buffer timings are development measurements; system load and thermal state can vary. No energy measurements were taken.
nextCandidates: Investigate FFT temporary-buffer layout to improve column-pass memory locality without changing butterfly arithmetic. Measure the full pipeline because a transpose can move costs between passes.
